nodes.name: O-doping by acidification
nodes.procedure: O-doped carbon black was prepared by acidification treatment of the pristine Vulcan XC-72 carbon black in nitric acid for 12 h (C-O-12) or 6 h (C-O-6).
nodes.source_text: We first prepared O-doped carbon black by acidification treatment of the pristine carbon black in nitric acid for 12h

nodes.name: F-doping by pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: F-doped carbon black was prepared by pyrolysis of PTFE nanopowder mixed with Vulcan XC-72 carbon black at 950°C under Ar/H2 gas flow. A representative F-doped carbon sample was derived from an initial mixture of 100 mg of carbon black and 800 mg of PTFE (C-F-800) or 400 mg of PTFE (C-F-400).

nodes.name: Electrode ink preparation and drop-casting
nodes.procedure: The carbon black samples (pristine, O-doped, or F-doped) were each mixed with commercial Pt/C nanoparticles (20% Pt on Vulcan XC-72) and Nafion solution (5 wt %) to form a uniform catalyst ink, which was drop-casted onto a piece of carbon substrate to form an electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt nanoparticles have average size of 3.0 ± 0.7 nm as shown by TEM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S1, the typical TEM image and corresponding particle size distribution reveal an average size of 3.0 ± 0.7 nm of the Pt nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey spectra show O 1s peak at ~532 eV increasing substantially in C-O-12 sample and F 1s peak at ~686 eV in C-F-800 sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS survey spectra of the three samples are presented in Figure 1d, with high-resolution XPS spectra of O 1s and F 1s peaks shown in Figure 1e and f, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows oxygen atomic percentage of 4.1% in pristine carbon black, 13.1% in C-O-12, and 3.1% fluorine in C-F-800.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) was used to roughly estimate the concentration of dopants. The atomic percentage of oxygen in the pristine carbon black is found to be 4.1%, which increases to 13.1% in the C-O-12 sample. While the pristine carbon black does not contain fluorine, the atom percentage of fluorine in the C-F-800 sample is around 3.1%.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images indicate that the Pt/C, Pt/C-O-12, and Pt/C-F-800 electrodes have similar morphology and porosity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a-c, the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images indicate that the three electrodes have a similar morphology and porosity, so the doped carbon has no noticeable impact on the electrode morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angles measured on electrodes: Pt/C 120.5°, Pt/C-O-12 77.4°, Pt/C-F-800 151.1°; post-N2H4 electro-oxidation: Pt/C 74.0°, Pt/C-O-12 19.7°, Pt/C-F-800 143.6°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2d-f, the Pt/C electrode exhibits a contact angle of 120.5° (Figure 2d) and the Pt/C-O-12 electrode is more hydrophilic with a smaller contact angle of 77.4° (Figure 2e), while the Pt/C-F-800 electrode is more hydrophobic with a larger contact angle of 151.1° (Figure 2f).
